scope: Theorem 1.1 (Limiting pressure) of the manuscript “All-temperature pressure for orthogonally invariant Ising spin glasses” (preprints/All-temperature-pressure-for-orthogonally-invariant-Ising-spin-glasses-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 234 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ecaeb31108feca6f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 2-3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let ΛN be deterministic real diagonal matrices whose empirical spectral measures converge weakly to a compactly supported probability law μ. Assume that their smallest and largest eigenvalues converge to the respective edges of supp μ. Let UN be Haar distributed 2 on O(N), and define PN using the uniform spin probability in Equation (1.1). With S and G1 as in Equations (1.7)–(1.8), lim N→∞ EPN = lim N→∞ PN = F(μ) := inf p∈P {S(p) + G1(p)}, (1.9) where the second limit holds almost surely. No independence of the matrices UN across dimensions is required.
